breeds.name: Xoloitzcuintli
breeds.also_known_as: Xoloitzcuintle (FCI's own spelling in FCI-St N°234, this row's actual cited primary-source standard); Mexican Hairless (AKC alias, still a separate unresolved worklist duplicate under key=mexican-hairless, same AKC source PDF)
breeds.estimate_note: Ni Leathlobhair et al. 2018 sequenced 71 mitochondrial + 7 nuclear genomes from ancient North American and Siberian dogs spanning ~9,000 years. All sampled precontact American dogs (PCDs) formed a monophyletic lineage descended from Siberian dogs introduced via early human migration(s) ~17,500-13,000 years ago, sharing a common ancestor ~14,600 years ago (95% HPD 16,484-12,965 ya) -- diverged from an ancestor shared with the Zhokhov Island dogs (see zhokhov-siberian-sled-dog) ~1,000 years earlier. Critically, this lineage was NOT domesticated locally from North American wolves. Corroborated by Perri et al. 2021 (PNAS), which independently found dogs accompanied the first people into the Americas as human dispersal began ~15,000 years ago -- consistent with this ~14,600-year figure via a different dataset/method.
breeds.breed_note: "Their origin dates far back in history" — eaten as a delicacy in pre-Hispanic Mexico in ceremonies, regarded as representative of the god Xolotl. No numeric date for that era.
breeds.notes: Added mrca_lineage_id 2026-08-09: Bergstrom et al. 2020 (Science) found ~3% pre-Columbian American dog ancestry survives in modern Xoloitzcuintle, tracing to the precontact American dog lineage dated by Ni Leathlobhair et al. 2018 (see mrca_lineage_id: precontact-american-dog) -- a minority-ancestry component, not proof the modern breed descends primarily from it. This breed still has no tier-2 (landrace) date of its own; confidence_tier corrected from anchor to vague to reflect that (was previously inconsistent with an empty origin_estimate_value -- confidence_tier describes tier-2 evidence quality specifically, per breed_origins_schema.md).

breeds.name: Taiwan Dog
breeds.estimate_note: Zhang et al. 2020 whole-genome analysis integrated a real Taiwan village dog sample with 97 published canid genomes; found it groups within a basal southern-East-Asia/Island-Southeast-Asia clade (the same clade that produced dingoes and New Guinea Singing Dogs), with clade divergence from Indonesian village dogs dated to ~9,900 years ago. Consistent with the broader <16,300-year regional dog-origin estimate south of the Yangtze River (Pang et al. 2009).
breeds.breed_note: FCI-St N°348 (2015): "originally native Taiwanese dogs, descendants of the South Asian hunting dogs which ancient local inhabitants used to live with." 1980 cooperative study (NTU/Gifu/Nagoya universities) confirmed South Asian hunting dog descent, no specific date.
breeds.notes: Downgraded from anchor to vague and origin_estimate cleared 2026-08-09: the ~9,900-year figure was a village-dog-population divergence date (Zhang et al. 2020, Taiwan/Indonesian basal clade), not a founding date for the modern standardized breed specifically -- conflating the two is the same ambiguity ancestor_lineages.csv was built to resolve, one tier over (population-level vs. breed-level, not MRCA-vs-breed, but the same principle). See village_dog_population_id for the (well-evidenced) population claim, which is unaffected by this change. Genuinely no separate landrace-tier date is known for the modern breed itself. Aggregator web claims of "10,000-20,000 years" remain unsourced regardless. See data/supplemental/taiwan-dog.txt for full research.

breeds.name: Siberian Husky
breeds.estimate_note: Sinding et al. 2020 sequenced a ~9,500-year-old dog genome from Zhokhov Island, northeastern Siberia (associated with early sled-dog technology) alongside 10 modern Greenland sled dogs; found Siberian Husky, Alaskan Malamute, and Greenland sled dog all share the major part of their genome with this ancient dog. Greenland sled dog shows the least admixture with other dog populations since this split -- the basis of its 'oldest/most original breed' reputation (Guinness World Records, 2020) -- a claim about genetic purity, not an earlier founding date than Husky or Malamute, which trace to the identical ancestor.
breeds.notes: Downgraded from anchor to vague and origin_estimate cleared 2026-08-09: the 9,500-year figure was an MRCA/ancestor-lineage date (Sinding et al. 2020, Zhokhov Island dog), not a Chukchi-specific founding date -- conflating the two is exactly the ambiguity ancestor_lineages.csv exists to resolve. See mrca_lineage_id for the (very well-evidenced) ancestor claim, which is unaffected by this change. Genuinely no separate landrace-tier date is known for this breed specifically.

breeds.name: Chow Chow
breeds.estimate_note: SECONDARY SOURCE, and a strong one: Wang et al. 2017, "The origin of chow chows in the light of the East Asian breeds," BMC Genomics — whole-genome sequencing of 9 Chow Chows plus 37 published canid genomes found the Chow Chow is one of the most basal (earliest-diverging) lineages among East Asian breeds (alongside Shar-Pei and Akita), diverging from the Chinese indigenous dog population approximately 8,300 years ago.
breeds.notes: Peer-reviewed genomic divergence-time estimate, not just an art/artifact claim — meaningfully stronger evidence than the Han Dynasty bas-relief lead mentioned in sources.md §3 (drop that lead in favor of this). Best-supported ancient-breed claim found in this whole research pass.

breeds.name: Akita
breeds.estimate_note: Gakuhari et al. 2015 directly AMS-radiocarbon-dated two dog burials excavated at the Kamikuroiwa rock shelter site (Shikoku, Japan), buried alongside a human individual -- calibrated age 7414-7273 calBP, the oldest confirmed dog burials in Japan. Masuda & Sato 2015 (companion mtDNA study of the same specimens) found one of the two dogs carried the M1 haplotype, also found in one ancient Okhotsk-period dog and eight animals across three modern Japanese indigenous breeds -- Shiba Inu, Akita, and Kishu -- plus four non-Japanese-breed animals.
breeds.notes: Downgraded from anchor to vague and origin_estimate cleared 2026-08-09: the previously-used "~5000 years ago" figure was an imprecise, uncited web-search paraphrase of the Kamikuroiwa Rock Shelter finding (see raw_extracts/akita.txt), not a breed-specific landrace date -- moved to mrca_lineage_id where it belongs, now with the actual peer-reviewed citations and the correct radiocarbon figure (~7,300-7,400 years ago, not ~5,000). Same tier-conflation pattern as Siberian Husky/Taiwan Dog. AKC's own page has no historical section beyond "ancient," so origin_estimate_note is left empty rather than filled with meta-commentary -- see mrca_lineage_id (kamikuroiwa-jomon-dog) for the real citations and finding. Genuinely no separate landrace-tier date is known for the modern standardized breed (formalized as a preservation effort in the early-to-mid 20th century).
